newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed in quiet trade Wednesday, with summer months down due to predictions of above-normal spring water levels boosting hydroelectric availability, industry sources said.
"There is not a lot of direction right now, but the summer months seem to have been impacted by forecasts of above normal (water) runoff levels," said futures a trader.
As of 1225 EST, March California Oregon Border (COB) was steady at $10.95 per megawatt hour (MWh), while April COB was bid at $10.05 and offered at $10.25 from a Tuesday settle at $10.20 per MWh.
June COB was down 15 cents at $10.85 per MWh.
March Palo Verde (PV) was off two cents at $13.20 after reaching as high as $13.30 per MWh, while April PV was bid at $12.40 from Tuesday's settle at $12.30 per MWh.
NYMEX March Henry Hub natural gas futures were down 10.8 cents at $2.116 per million British thermal units.
As of 1200 EST, NYMEX said an estimated two COB and 62 PV contracts had traded.
Although water level predictions were putting some downward pressure on contracts, traders said they expected the contracts to stay within their recent ranges due to a lack of news.

In the Northwest, temperatures are forecast to average three to six degrees Fahrenheit above normal through Friday with peak readings in the 30s-40s. Showers are expected to continue across the coast while valley rain and mountain snow were called for in the interior regions.

In the Southwest, temperatures will likely stay two to four degrees below normal ahead of the weekend with day readings reaching the 50-60 degree range. An area of low pressure in the southeastern area of the region could cause precipitation through early Thursday.
Separately, restart of a 755 megawatt (MW) unit 4 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico was pushed back to today after tripping off line Sunday.
The 1,100 MW pumped storage hydroelectric Helms plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut Feb 1 for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for another week.
A 330 MW unit at the coal-fired Colstrip generating facility near Billings, Montana, was reportedly shut Monday for repairs, and expected to resume operation today.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear plant in Richland, Wash., trimmed its output overnight to 65 percent power after a recirculation pump trip.
COB open interest for Feb 11 rose 25 to 3,555, while PV open interest fell 58 to 1,657, NYMEX said.
